newsitem.title: JAPAN: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - Jan 8.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - Jan 8.

text.p: Leading life and non-life insurance companies plan to introduce new products this autumn following the insurance agreement between Japan and the United States late last year.
Non-life insurers, including Tokio Marine & Fire Insurance Co Ltd, plan to sell auto insurance by mail, while life insurers may sell medical coverage.

Yokogawa Electric Corp and Yamatake-Honeywell Co Ltd are expecting better business results for the business year to March 31 due to a recovery in public-sector demand for plant control systems and internal cost-cutting efforts. Yokogawa predicts a four percent increase in sales to 180 billion yen and a 66 percent increase in pre-tax profit to six billion yen from a year ago, while Yamatake-Honeywell sees a 17 percent increase in pre-tax profit to 4.4 billion yen and a four percent increase in sales to 114 billion yen.

Alpine Electronics Inc is expected to post about 2.3 billion yen in consolidated net profit in the year to March 31, up 190 percent from a year ago. This is due to steady shipments of audio systems for cars in domestic and overseas markets and the weaker yen which boosts revenues at foreign units.

Microsoft Co Ltd, the Japanese unit of Microsoft Corp, will stop recommending retail prices for its products in Japan from February 1, as market prices for computer software are far lower than current recommended prices due to cutthroat competition. Microsoft will shift to open pricing.

Kawasaki Kisen Kaisha Ltd, China Ocean Shipping (Group) Co (COSCO) and Yang Ming Marine Transport Corp plan to set up a consortium to launch a weekly Atlantic Ocean container service from late February.
Canon Inc plans to develop ink-jet printers in Taiwan for the Asian market, and begin mass production of the products in the region by the end of this year.
